clue.text: A dim old animal, I fear lengthy verbs aren't to be: borrow replacements

definitions.text: A dim old animal, I fear lengthy verbs aren't to be: borrow replacements

indicators.note: replacements tells us the letters of the words before it are moved into new places to make the quotation

parts.words: A dim old animal, I fear lengthy verbs aren't to be: borrow

explanation.surface: A slow-witted elderly creature admits that long words frighten it and asks for simpler stand-ins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the anagram fodder and also describes the speaker: Winnie-the-Pooh, the dim old bear of A. A. Milne's stories, who says this line about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooh, a slow-witted toy bear, describes himself with this famous line, so the clue's portrait of a dim beast scared of long verbs fits it.

clue.text: Feeding installation sustains a runner

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up or support, so the outer word holds the inner letter within it

parts.note: a manger is a trough that animals feed from

explanation.surface: Some piece of farm equipment for feeding is keeping an athlete going.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner can mean someone who runs a business or team, the person in charge of it.

clue.text: Weapon's bullet's lead — and it hurts!

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so we take only the opening letter of bullet's

parts.note: ow is the cry you give when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone describes being shot: the front of the bullet arrives, and it is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Weapon's' stands for 'Weapon is', with the 's as the link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer's bow is a weapon that shoots arrows.

clue.text: Snap at grasping little brother going up to London?

indicators.note: grasping means holding tight, so the word at closes around the other letters

parts.note: br is the short form of brother
in British usage you go up to London, so the direction word is up

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a younger brother who is heading for London.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelling to London, or to a university, is called going UP in British English, however you approach it.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap as an adjective means sudden, without warning, the same as a curt or unannounced action.

clue.text: Caucasian is unusually large, determined man

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the label for unusually large clothes
set means fixed or determined, as in a set date
Ian is a common man's name

explanation.surface: Someone describes a white man as remarkably big and resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caucasian' looks like it means white; here it means from the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ossetians are a people of the Caucasus region, between Russia and Georgia.

clue.text: Statue after shattering lies unmoved

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters that follow are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Even after being smashed, a statue lies there without moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous armless ancient Greek marble figure in the Louvre.

clue.text: Keen on following race meet

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first, so the race word comes first

parts.note: to race is to run
into is slang for keen on, as in into jazz

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for racing tags along behind a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: See 1
Six sixes have both two and four of these

definitions.text: Six sixes have both two and four of these

parts.words: Six sixes have both two and four of these
parts.note: six times six is thirty-six, which is four times nine; and the numeral 66 turned upside down shows two of the figure 9

explanation.surface: A puzzle about numbers asks what six sixes contain twice and four times.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty-six divided by nine is four, and an inverted 66 reads as a pair of the digit after eight.

clue.text: Add dull report about me turning reactionary

parts.note: to stick in is to add or insert something

indicators.note: about means around, so the dull report surrounds the turned word

parts.note: a thud is a dull heavy sound

indicators.note: turning means the word me is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to add a dull account of their own reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add' reads as STICK IN, to insert something; 'turning' reverses 'me', and 'about' wraps the dull report around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud resists change, which is what a reactionary person does.

clue.text: Coin producer keeps it in circulation

indicators.note: something in circulation goes round, so the run of letters is read backwards
the word producer keeps the answer inside it, holding it in its middle letters

explanation.surface: A mint keeps its coins circulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps it' gives UCE from inside 'producer', and 'in circulation' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecu was an old French coin, and also the name of the European currency unit before the euro.

clue.text: Finishes off most of the drink over club

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill or finish them off

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its last letter, so the word loses its end

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone drains the last of a drink before heading off to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPS, TH (most of 'the') and GIN make TOPSTHGIN, which 'over' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub, a place for evening entertainment, is a club.

clue.text: Bit of a storm after high-tension I don't secure doors adequately?

indicators.note: after places the high letter behind the tension letter rather than in the order the clue gives them

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for tension
read whimsically as I underbolt, meaning I fit too few bolts

explanation.surface: Someone admits poor home security after a tense stormy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts H (high) behind T (tension). UNDERBOLT is a made-up verb meaning to bolt too little.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash of lightning with its crash of thunder is one part of a storm.

clue.text: Branch of religion from just south of Canada to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading from right to left, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: just south of Canada is in the northern US: IN, N for northern, US

explanation.surface: A faith spreads westward from the states along the Canadian border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just south of Canada' gives IN N US, and 'to the west' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunni are the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Desperate, putting on front of Harpers and Queen Anne Robinson's party

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Harpers is used

parts.note: a queen signs as Regina, so Queen Anne is Anne Regina, AR
Peter Robinson led the Democratic Unionist Party, DUP, in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a glossy-magazine party hosted by a TV presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpers and Queen was a British society magazine, and Anne Robinson is a TV quiz host: both are decoys. The DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up means short of money, in a desperate position.

clue.text: Site linking friends and advice for the work shy?

explanation.surface: A social website also offers tips for people who avoid their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A social network website connecting friends; read as two words, telling a shy person to confront the work (book).

clue.text: See 1
Sweet, soft cure for otitis?

parts.note: p is the music abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
otitis is an ear infection, treated with ear drops

explanation.surface: A gentle treatment for an ear infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a boiled sweet with a fruity pear flavour, a British confectionery.

clue.text: African people making for Forest, perhaps, swapping parts

clue.text: Prime minister and players conducted victory tours

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the victory word goes around the players

parts.note: a win is a victory
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, players led by a conductor

explanation.surface: A premier and a band are taken on a victory tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was a British prime minister in the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson led the UK government twice, serving as its prime minister.

clue.text: Does it enable creatures to climb for long time?

definitions.text: Does it enable creatures to climb for long time?

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: animats are artificial creatures, robots modelled on animals

explanation.surface: A question about what keeps animals climbing for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power or endurance is what lets anything keep going for a long while.

clue.text: I have partner's hamper

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'I have partner's hamper (6)': 'hamper' defines it and PAIR is partner, but 'I have' does not give IM, so the wordplay as printed does not build the letters

clue.text: Flower in the divine mould orchid? Not quite?

indicators.note: to mould is to reshape, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement
not quite the whole word means its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a moulded orchid is a divine flower, not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, not a bloom: ichor was the fluid in the veins of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, ichor was the fluid that ran through the gods' veins in place of blood.

clue.text: In no way will his treatment work?

definitions.text: In no way will his treatment work?

parts.words: In no way will his treatment work?
parts.note: a sceptic's jibe at a practitioner of a therapy of highly diluted remedies, which critics say cannot work

explanation.surface: A doubter claims that some therapist's methods can never succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics say homeopathic remedies are diluted until nothing of the active ingredient remains.

clue.text: Working party to have existence slightly extended

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Working party to have existence slightly extended (3)': 'Working party' defines it and 'to have existence' is BE, but no clue word supplies the extra E, so it reads as a cryptic hint that the check cannot parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Working party to have existence slightly extended

clue.text: Crackers, Gorgonzola sandwiches

indicators.note: the word Gorgonzola sandwiches the answer, holding it between its outer letters

explanation.surface: Cheese and crackers: Gorgonzola served in sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonzo is slang for crazy or bizarre, like crackers.

clue.text: Economic policy is in 2 reforming pieces

indicators.note: the pieces are re-formed, put together in a new shape, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer of clue 2 down

explanation.surface: An economic programme is said to be the work of a manager reshaping parts.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' stands for the answer to 2 down, MANAGER; its letters with IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaganomics, the free-market programme of US President Ronald Reagan in the 1980s.

clue.text: Take seconds in catching and ring bird

indicators.note: take the second letter in each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A bird is caught and ringed in a matter of seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ani is a black tropical American cuckoo.
